record_type_quote:
Objective To replicate this association in an independent population with a different genetic

background.

targets.authors: Sanna S, Pitzalis M, Zoledziewska M, Zara I, Sidore C, Murru R, Whalen MB, Busonero F, Maschio A, Costa G, Melis MC, Deidda F, Poddie F, Morelli L, Farina G, Li Y, Dei M, Lai S, Mulas A, Cuccuru G, Porcu E, Liang L, Zavattari P, Moi L, Deriu E, Urru MF, Bajorek M, Satta MA, Cocco E, Ferrigno P, Sotgiu S, Pugliatti M, Traccis S, Angius A, Melis M, Rosati G, Abecasis GR, Uda M, Marrosu MG, Schlessinger D, Cucca F
targets.evidence_quote:
Recently, a novel association with risk for MS of some

markers within the CBLB gene (Cas-Br-M (murine) ecotropic retroviral transforming sequence b,

3q13.11) was observed in the island population from Sardinia.[6]

Hence we tested the positive association observed with the T allele of the top associated variant

(rs9657904) observed in the Sardinian study in a large cohort of continental MS patients and controls.
targets.outcome_quote:
The same allele (T) of rs9657904 SNP, positively associated with MS in Sardinian population, was

significantly associated with MS risk (one tailed p = 7.35 x 10-5 ), and even showed a comparable effect

size (OR = 1.31) also in the Italian mainland (Table 1).
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly compare the same risk allele and report significant association with comparable effect size in the independent mainland sample.

reasoning: Full manuscript with references acquired from HAL; title, authors and printed assigned DOI verify identity. The appended Table 1 wording in supplied metadata does not identify a different work. Introduction cites reference 6 for the Sardinian CBLB association and then states that this association is tested. Reference 6 is Sanna et al. (2010); its entry supplies neither title nor DOI, so these are blank. Later discussion erroneously labels the Sardinian study [5]; this is recorded as a citation-number inconsistency, not a second target, because the introduction explicitly links the tested CBLB finding to [6].
